candidate_relations.reason: The tumor was desmin/SMA positive but CD117 and DOG-1 negative, opposing a gastrointestinal stromal tumor.
Only 2% Ki-67 and hormone-receptor positivity support indolent disseminated leiomyomatosis rather than leiomyosarcoma.
Biopsy showed smooth muscle rather than adenocarcinoma, and the rectosigmoid relationship was extrinsic.
The multinodular pelvic disease persisted after right adnexectomy and was histologically smooth-muscle tissue.
Rectal mucosa was smooth and the mass compressed the bowel from the pelvic cavity.
Diffuse peritoneal nodules expressing desmin, SMA, ER, and PR do not establish a solitary fibrous tumor.
Both canonical GIST markers, CD117 and DOG-1, were negative in the sampled smooth-muscle tumor.
Her recurrent endometriomas and pelvic operations support endometriosis, but the reference also requires disseminated leiomyomatosis.
Low-proliferation smooth-muscle histology and prior adnexectomy do not support ovarian carcinoma.
Multiple peritoneal nodules after hysterectomy extend beyond a leiomyoma confined to the uterus.
